ecological_question: Across neighboring Palmer Archipelago breeding islands, is penguin functional differentiation generated mainly by species turnover, or does a persistent within-species island phenotype remain after restricting to Adelie penguins?

three_year_hypotheses.H1_turnover: Archipelago-scale morphology-to-island predictability is dominated by species composition rather than persistent within-species island morphology.
three_year_hypotheses.H2_persistent_island: Persistent Adelie island phenotypes should produce fixed island effects after controlling sex, year, laying date and clutch completion.
three_year_hypotheses.H3_temporal_reassembly: Temporally labile colony states should produce island-by-year structure and reversals of pairwise island contrasts.
three_year_hypotheses.H4_cross_year_transfer: Persistent island phenotypes should classify held-out-year Adelie individuals above the one-third balanced-accuracy reference.

longterm_primary_question: Does long-term functional change on Antarctic breeding islands occur mainly through changes in species composition and abundance rather than inferred within-species morphological change?

longterm_rules.missing_species_record: exclude island-year; do not silently convert to zero
longterm_rules.primary_between_year_transition: same contributing site coverage in both years
longterm_rules.species_not_known_to_breed_at_site: structural zero allowed using APBP site_species membership

interpretation_boundaries: No evolutionary local-adaptation claim from these observational data.
No individual-plasticity claim from island-by-year structural trait differences because different adults were sampled.
Body mass is condition-sensitive and is reported separately from structural traits.
Blood stable isotopes integrate pre-breeding foraging and are not local summer island-foraging measurements.
Community-weighted historical morphology initially uses fixed species trait centroids; it quantifies assembly-driven functional change, not historical trait evolution.

rationale: Pygoscelis penguins forage at sea but reproduce on land, so the breeding island does not contain the main trophic resource base.
Island occupancy and breeding performance can therefore be strongly filtered by snow-free nesting area, geomorphology, precipitation and access to the marine foraging landscape.
Direct biotic interactions are not assumed absent: nest-site competition can occur locally and marine foraging niches can overlap or partition.
Penguins also transport marine nutrients onto land and alter soils and terrestrial microbial/plant communities, so they are ecosystem engineers as well as island occupants.
ecological_system.island_ecology_contrast: Unlike many terrestrial island communities, local food-web interactions and resource production are partly externalized to the surrounding ocean while breeding habitat is spatially discrete on land.

special_system_hypotheses.E1_abiotic_first_breeding_filter: If terrestrial trophic interactions are secondary at the island scale, colony persistence and reassembly should track snow, geomorphology and regional sea-ice forcing more strongly than local heterospecific abundance.
special_system_hypotheses.E2_localized_biotic_interaction: Where species share nesting space, heterospecific abundance may matter through nest-site competition; this should be strongest in mixed or spatially overlapping colonies rather than as a universal island-wide effect.
special_system_hypotheses.E3_marine_partitioning: Coexisting species may reduce trophic competition by spatial or temporal partitioning of marine foraging areas, decoupling local terrestrial coexistence from a single shared island food resource.
special_system_hypotheses.E4_biovector_feedback: Colony abundance should modify the terrestrial island environment through marine-derived nutrient deposition, creating a feedback from penguin community composition to soils, vegetation and microbial communities.
special_system_hypotheses.E5_externalized_resource_island_biogeogr: For these central-place marine foragers, effective island quality should depend on ice-free breeding habitat and access to marine resources, not only classical island area and isolation.

candidate_biotic_predictors: heterospecific nest abundance at shared breeding sites
candidate_abiotic_predictors: snow persistence or snow-free nesting area
